vocabulary.meaning_en: a word that adds information to a verb, an adjective or another adverb
vocabulary.example: In "He spoke calmly", "calmly" is an adverb.

vocabulary.meaning_en: extra strength on a word or idea

vocabulary.example: He wore a brightly coloured jacket.
He moved rather slowly for a young man.

vocabulary.meaning_ar: في الداخل / حول / في كل مكان

vocabulary.meaning_en: not often (a little more than rarely; mostly in books)

vocabulary.example: She habitually drinks tea in the morning.

fine_lines.title: adjective vs adverb
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الصفة تصف الاسم (a bright jacket). الظرف يصف الفعل أو الصفة أو ظرفًا آخر (brightly coloured). أغلب الظروف تنتهي بـ ly، لكن بعض الصفات أيضًا تنتهي بـ ly (friendly).
fine_lines.explanation_en: An adjective describes a noun (a bright jacket). An adverb describes a verb, an adjective or another adverb (brightly coloured). Most adverbs end in -ly, but some adjectives do too (friendly).

examples.sentence: She has a brightly coloured jacket.

fine_lines.title: seldom vs rarely
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلاهما بمعنى "نادرًا". rarely = تقريبًا أبدًا وهو الأكثر استعمالًا في الكلام. seldom أكثر قليلًا من rarely ويظهر في كتب القواعد.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean "not often". "Rarely" = almost never and is more common in speech. "Seldom" is a little more often than rarely and appears in grammar books.

examples.sentence: We seldom go to the cinema.

expressions.meaning_en: You speak faster than I can follow.
expressions.example: Please slow down. You speak too quickly.
Your keys? Look inside your bag.
The old bus moved rather slowly.

grammar.title: 1) Adverbs modify verbs: where, how, when
grammar.explanation_ar: الظرف الذي يصف الفعل يخبرنا أين (inside, around, everywhere) وكيف (quickly, calmly) ومتى (yesterday, today, tomorrow). ويأتي عادةً بعد الفعل.
grammar.explanation_en: An adverb that modifies a verb tells us where (inside, around, everywhere), how (quickly, calmly) and when (yesterday, today, tomorrow). It usually comes after the verb.

grammar.title: Adverbs of frequency come BEFORE the verb
grammar.explanation_ar: ظروف التكرار (الأخوات السبع): always (100%) – usually – often – sometimes (50%) – seldom – rarely – never (0%). تأتي قبل الفعل الرئيسي: I usually go وليس I go usually.
grammar.explanation_en: Adverbs of frequency (the seven sisters): always (100%) – usually – often – sometimes (50%) – seldom – rarely – never (0%). They go before the main verb: "I usually go", not "I go usually".
examples: I always go to the gym on Monday.

grammar.title: 2) Adverbs intensify adjectives
grammar.explanation_ar: الظرف قبل الصفة يقويها ويعطيها شدة: very hot, very cold, brightly coloured.
grammar.explanation_en: An adverb before an adjective makes it stronger: very hot, very cold, brightly coloured.

grammar.title: 3) Adverbs give emphasis to other adverbs
grammar.explanation_ar: الظرف قبل ظرف آخر يعطيه توكيدًا: too quickly, too slowly, rather slowly.
grammar.explanation_en: An adverb before another adverb adds emphasis: too quickly, too slowly, rather slowly.

grammar.title: -ly: the most common adverb ending
grammar.explanation_ar: أغلب الظروف تُصنع بإضافة ly إلى الصفة: quick → quickly, normal → normally, regular → regularly.
grammar.explanation_en: Most adverbs are made by adding -ly to an adjective: quick → quickly, normal → normally, regular → regularly.

questions.question: Adverbs can modify verbs, adjectives and ___.
questions.explanation_ar: الظرف يصف الفعل والصفة وظرفًا آخر.
questions.explanation_en: Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives and other adverbs.

questions.question: When an adverb modifies a verb, it tells us ___.
Choose the correct sentence.
choices: I go usually to the gym.
I usually go to the gym.
Usually I go usually to the gym.
I go to usually the gym.
questions.explanation_en: The frequency adverb goes before the verb.
